Title: Get started
Summary: From a chart photo to corrected images in eight steps.

Items: You have photos taken under fixed lighting, and one of them shows a color chart. You want every photo's colors to match what the chart says they should be.
chart-split

A real result. Left: ColorCard_Big.JPG as photographed. Right: the same chart after FFC, GC, WB and the default Root polynomial CC, with Blank.JPG as the white reference. The mean ΔE00 fell from 7.05 to 1.26.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: **Add photos.** Drag JPEG, PNG or TIFF files onto the window, or choose **Files** or **Folder** under Add media (`Ctrl+O`, `Ctrl+Shift+O`). They join the **Session**.

**Select the chart photo.** The app looks for a chart when you select a photo. Press **Detect** in the Chart section to run it again. If the photo holds more than one chart, choose one under **Chart face**.
**Check the overlay.** The outline should sit on the chart, with one cell per patch. Turn on **Lattice** or **Sample** in the strip on the preview for a closer look.
**Optional: add a white reference** for flat-field correction. See “Flat-field correction (FFC)”.
**Choose stages.** Under **Process**, tick FFC, GC, WB and CC. Turn off any stage you do not need.
**Press Fit + apply** (`F5`). The app learns a model from the chart and corrects this photo.
**Check the result.** Compare the Original and Corrected tabs above the preview, then read the **ΔE Analysis** below it.
**Save.** Press `Ctrl+S`, tick the photos and outputs you want, choose a folder under Save to, and press **Save selected**.
run-mock
The run area at the bottom of the left panel. The main button says Fit + apply when it will learn a new model, and Apply model when it will reuse the loaded one.

Sections.Heading: What you will see
Items: The stage chips above the run button light up one after another: FFC, SAT (saturation), GC, WB, CC and Save result. Stages you turned off stay dim.
The session tile shows what was detected, for example a chart type, or “no chart”.
The status bar shows the fitted mean ΔE00. Lower is better.
A finished preview is not a saved file. Nothing is written to your folder until you press **Save selected**.

Sections.Heading: Correct more photos with the same model
Items: Open **Model** in the left panel and choose **Use loaded**. The main button changes to **Apply model**.
Select a photo from the same setup and press **Apply model**. That photo does not need a chart.
For many photos at once, use **Batch** (`Ctrl+B`).

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: Fit + apply is greyed out|Read the hint under the button. It names what is missing, for example “Detect the chart, then Fit + apply.”
The tile says “no chart”|See “Troubleshooting”. The blank white photo is never a chart; select a photo that shows the chart.
Colors look worse after correction|Check that the photo and the chart were taken under the same light and exposure, then read “Reading the ΔE analysis”.

Title: How correction works
Summary: Five stages, in a fixed order, each with its own input.

Items: You want to know what each stage does, so you can decide which ones to turn on.
pipeline
Stages always run in this order. Each stage sees the result of the stages before it.

Sections.Heading: The stages
Items: **FFC · Flat field** evens out lighting across the frame. It multiplies lightness (L*) by a smooth gain map learned from a blank white photo.
**Saturation** estimates the true color of chart patches that the camera clipped. **Skip saturated patches** under Process turns this step off.
**GC · Tone response** fits a lightness curve from the chart's grey patches.
**WB · White balance** scales the red, green and blue channels so the grey patches come out neutral.
**CC · Color fit** maps the remaining color errors with the model you choose under CC settings.
stage-bars
Mean ΔE00 on the chart after each stage, from the ColorCard_Big.JPG fit. GC and CC did most of the work here; your setup may differ.
In the default fast mode, GC, WB and CC are folded into one 65×65×65 lookup table and FFC runs in the same pass. The GPU is used when it is faster. See “Speed: devices and modes”.
A saved model stores GC, WB and CC. FFC is spatial: when it is on, Apply model recomputes it from the white reference, so it needs the blank white photo and the same framing.

Title: Flat-field correction (FFC)
Summary: Remove uneven lighting with a blank white photo.

Items: The center of your photos is brighter than the corners, so the same color reads differently across the frame. You want even lighting before color correction.
ffc

Top left: the white area of Blank.JPG, with its contrast stretched so the fall-off shows. Faint marks on the surface show too. Top right: the smooth gain map that flattens it, up to ×1.09 at the corners. Below: lightness across the middle of the frame, before and after the gain.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: **Take a white reference.** Photograph a clean, matte, blank white surface that fills the frame. Use the same camera position, lens, exposure, lighting and image size as your other photos.
**Add it to the app.** Add it to the Session or a Catalog folder like any other photo.
**Make it the white reference.** Drag it onto the white well under **FFC · Flat field**, click the **W** badge on its Catalog tile, or press **White file**.
**Tick FFC · Flat field** and press **Fit + apply**.
**Check the area used.** Turn on **Plane** in the strip on the preview to see which part of the white photo the app used.

Sections.Heading: Choosing a good white reference
Items: Good: the same setup and framing, a uniform matte surface, nothing clipped to pure white.
Avoid: the chart photo itself, objects or labels in the frame, dust, glare, or a different zoom or crop.
One white reference serves every photo taken in that setup. Take a new one when the lights, the camera or the framing change.

Sections.Heading: FFC settings
Items: The gear button next to FFC opens **FFC settings**. **Fit method** is Linear, Polynomial (the default), PLS or Neural net. You can also set **Sampling grid** (4–200), **Smoothing window** (odd, 1–51) and **Polynomial degree** (1–7). A higher degree is not automatically more accurate; start with the defaults.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: Rings, blotches or dark corners after FFC|The white photo probably has marks, objects or edges in it, or a different framing. Retake it, or compare with FFC turned off.
FFC is rejected for your input|FFC, GC and WB need sRGB/D65 input. Convert other inputs first, or run CC alone.

Title: Tone (GC) and white balance
Summary: Learned automatically from the chart's grey patches.

Items: Your photos are too dark, too flat or tinted, and you want the greys of the chart to come out at the right lightness and perfectly neutral.
gc

The six grey patches of ColorCard_Big.JPG. Hollow dots are their lightness as photographed; filled dots are after correction. Points on the diagonal match the chart's reference values. The swatches show the same greys before and after: note the blue tint that WB removes.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: Tick **GC · Tone response** and **WB · White balance** under Process.
Press **Fit + apply**.
Open the GC and WB tabs above the preview to see each stage's effect.

Sections.Heading: What the app does
Items: **GC** compares the measured lightness of the chart's named grey patches (after FFC, if it is on) with their reference lightness. It fits a smooth curve that only rises, anchored at black and white. It is not a single gamma number, and it has no settings. The ⓘ button next to GC explains this.
GC needs at least two usable grey patches.
**WB** sets one gain each for red, green and blue so that those grey patches become neutral.
**Apply model** reuses the saved curve and gains. New photos do not need a chart.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: The light grey patches are clipped or show glare|Retake the chart with less exposure or without the reflection. Correction cannot recover detail the camera did not record.
Highlights look flat after GC|Check the Patch ΔE table. A clipped white patch is marked in the Sat column.

Title: Choosing a color model (CC)
Summary: Simple models generalise; flexible models can overfit.

Items: You want the most accurate colors on new photos, not only on the chart you fitted.
cc-models
How the CC methods compare. Flexibility helps on hard lighting but needs more patches to stay honest. Ratings are guidance, not measurements.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: Press the gear button next to **CC · Color fit**. This opens **Correction settings**.
Choose a **Method**. Start with **Root polynomial** (the default) at degree 2.
Press **Fit + apply**, then note the CC-only validation line in the ΔE Analysis tab.
Try one step more and one step less flexible. Keep the simplest method whose validation ΔE is close to the best.

Sections.Heading: The methods, honestly
Items: **3x3 CCM**: nine numbers. Very stable and predictable, but it cannot fix errors that bend differently in shadows and highlights.
**Root polynomial** (root degree 2 or 3): the default. Its terms scale with brightness, so it copes well when exposure varies a little. A good first choice.
**Polynomial regression** (degree 1–7, optional combination terms): flexible. High degrees can fit 24 patches almost perfectly and still fail on new photos.
**PLS** (N components, 0 = auto): a regularised regression that copes with many related terms. Fewer components means a smoother fit.

**Neural net**: the most flexible and the slowest to fit. It overfits a 24-patch chart easily. Hidden layers takes one width or up to four, such as `100`, `100, 30` or `[128, 64, 32]` (each 4–512). Optimizer is Adam, SGD · momentum or RMSProp. Dropout runs from 0 to 0.8; 0 turns it off.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: Fit mean is tiny but validation is much higher|The model is memorising the chart. Choose a simpler method or a lower degree.
Vivid colors clip or shift after a flexible fit|Compare with Root polynomial. Check saturated patches in the Patch ΔE table.
Correction settings also hold the color spaces, the output format, Export training data, Chart references… and Reset all processing settings.

Title: Reading the ΔE analysis
Summary: How close the corrected chart is to its reference, and how far to trust it.

Items: You want to know whether a correction is good enough, and which colors are still off.
de-scale
The words the app shows next to a ΔE00 value. The swatch pairs differ by exactly the ΔE00 shown, so you can see roughly what each step looks like.
metric-mock
The summary cards from the ColorCard_Big.JPG fit. The large number is after correction; the small number is before.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: Open **ΔE Analysis** below the preview. Drag the divider above it upward for more room.
Read **Fit mean ΔE**, **Median ΔE** and **Max ΔE**. A low mean with a high max means a few patches are still wrong.
Read the validation line, for example “CC-only validation · 5-fold mean 2.21”. It holds patches out of the fit, so it is a fairer estimate than the fit mean.
Open **Chart rendition** to compare each patch with its reference, and open **Patch ΔE table** for the numbers.
Use **Export** on any plot card to save it as an image.
rendition
Each tile: left half as photographed, right half corrected, bottom strip the reference color. Taken from the same fit.

Sections.Heading: What the numbers mean
Items: ΔE00 (CIEDE2000) is a perceptual color difference in CIELAB. Around 1 is barely visible side by side; above 5 is clearly different.
**Per stage** and **CIEDE2000 by stage** show how much each stage helped.
Validation tests the CC fit only: GC and WB are fitted before the folds. It is not a test on an independent photo. To test the whole pipeline, photograph a second chart and evaluate it.
Photos corrected with Apply model have no chart to measure, so the app shows no ΔE for them.
Published reference values cannot certify your individual chart. Aging, dirt, printing variation, glare and the light's spectrum still add uncertainty.

Title: Models: save, load, .cube
Summary: Reuse a correction without a chart, or take it to other software.

Items: You fitted a good model and want to use it again later, on another computer, or in an editor that reads 3D LUTs.
model-mock
The Model section of the left panel.

Sections.Heading: Save and load
Items: After **Fit + apply**, the new model is loaded. The Model section shows its summary.
Press **Save** and choose a file name. The model is saved as JSON, together with the chart reference values it used.
Later, press **Load** and pick the JSON. The app switches to **Use loaded**, and the main button becomes **Apply model**.
Choosing **Fit from image** and pressing **Fit + apply** trains a new model, which replaces the loaded one. Save first if you want to keep it.

Sections.Heading: Export a .cube LUT
Items: With a model loaded, press **.cube** and choose where to save it.
The app writes a 33-point 3D LUT with GC, WB and CC. The status bar confirms: “Exported .cube (LUT does not include flat-field).”
Load the .cube in software that reads 3D LUTs. Feed it photos in the same encoding the model was fitted on.

Sections.Heading: Good to know
Items: A LUT cannot hold FFC, because FFC changes with position in the frame. For FFC, apply the model in this app with the white reference.
A model only transfers to photos from the same camera, lighting, exposure and settings. If any of these change, fit again.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: “Could not save … Choose another folder.”|The folder is read-only or full. Save to a folder you can write to.
Load, Save or .cube is greyed out|Wait for the current operation to finish. Save and .cube need a fitted or loaded model.

Title: Batch processing
Summary: Correct many photos in one run.

Items: You have many photos from the same setup and want them all corrected, without pressing Apply model on each one.
sample-split
Sample_3572.JPG corrected with the model fitted on ColorCard_Big.JPG. Left half as photographed, right half corrected.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: Add the photos to the Session. A session holds up to 80 photos.
Press **Batch** next to the run button (`Ctrl+B`).
Tick the photos to process. White references and files ending in _corrected start unticked.
Leave **Preview results** on to see each result as it finishes. Turn it off to skip the previews and go faster.
Press **Apply current model** to reuse the loaded model; these photos need no chart. Or press **Fit from chart** to detect a chart and fit a separate model for each selected photo.
When the batch ends, press `Ctrl+S` and **Save selected** to export the results.
batch-mock
The Batch panel.

Sections.Heading: What you will see
Items: The stage chips follow the current photo. **Batch progress** below them follows the whole queue.
The percentage counts finished work, not time. Some stages take longer than others.
In fast mode, GC, WB and CC run together in one pass, so their chips light up together.
With previews off, a finished photo shows “Result ready · Preview off”. **Show preview** opens just that one.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: You need to stop|Press **Cancel**. Finished photos keep their results.
One photo fails|The others still finish. The Log tab names the photo and the reason.
Batch is greyed out|Add photos to the Session first, and wait for any running operation to finish.

Title: Speed: devices and modes
Summary: Auto device choice, the detection engine, and fast vs compatibility mode.

Items: You want faster processing, or you need results that match an older version exactly.
device-mock
Processing settings, with Advanced expanded.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: Click **Processing settings** under the app name at the top left (`Ctrl+Alt+A`).
**Image correction** is Auto (recommended), CPU or GPU. Auto chooses for you, and the CPU takes over if needed.

Under **Advanced**, **Detection engine** chooses how charts are found: Auto (recommended), CPU, WebGPU, DirectML (Windows only) or Vulkan. Press **Apply engine change** afterwards. This restarts the engine.
Tick **Compatibility mode** only to reproduce older results.
Under **Device details**, **Check setup** rescans your hardware. **Use CPU** sets both detection and correction to the CPU.
modes
Fast mode (the default) builds one lookup table and corrects every pixel in a single pass. Compatibility mode runs each stage separately: slower, and results may differ very slightly.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: A forced GPU engine reports an error|Choose Auto or CPU and press Apply engine change. Auto recovers on the CPU; a forced engine reports the problem instead.

Acceleration is missing|Under Device details choose a setup mode (Recommended, CPU only or Custom) and press **Install optional support**. Graphics drivers come from your system or GPU vendor, not from this app.

Title: Sessions and files
Summary: The working set, the catalog, saved sessions and moved photos.

Items: You want to organise your photos, come back to the work later, and recover when files move.

Sections.Heading: Session and Catalog
Items: The **Session** is your working set, up to 80 photos. When it is full, extra photos are not added and the Log says so.
The **Catalog** lists folders you keep an eye on. Press **Watch folder** to add one. Click a tile to add it to the Session, or drag it in. Use **Filter by name…** to search.
Ctrl-click selects several tiles, Shift-click selects a range. The **W** badge marks the FFC white reference.
The large arrows beside the preview, or `Alt+Left` and `Alt+Right`, move between photos. The tabs above the preview switch stages, not photos.
Hover the preview to read RGB and Lab under the pointer. Right-click to copy them, and press `Esc` to clear.

Sections.Heading: Save and reopen your work
Items: Press `Ctrl+Shift+S` (or the save icon by Session) to save the session.
Press `Ctrl+Alt+O` (or the load icon) to open it again. Its photos, chart detections and results come back with it.
`Delete` removes the selected photos from the Session. It never deletes your files.

Sections.Heading: If something goes wrong
Items: A tile says the image is unavailable|The file was moved or deleted. Select the tile and press **Relink image…** (or right-click the tile) to find it. If the content matches, its detection and results are kept; a different file needs Detect again.
“Settings could not be saved”|The settings folder is not writable. Changes still apply until you close the app.

Title: Troubleshooting
Summary: Common problems, what the app says, and what to do.

Sections.Heading: Detection
Items: No chart detected (“no chart”)|Make sure the whole chart is in the frame, in focus, evenly lit and free of glare. Then press **Retry**. If it still fails, set Detection engine to CPU, press Apply engine change, and try again.
The wrong chart or face is used|Pick the right one under **Chart face**. Turn on **Lattice** to check the patch order before fitting.

Sections.Heading: Files
Items: A photo was moved, renamed or deleted|Select its tile and press **Relink image…**. See “Sessions and files”.
“The image is … over the 200 MP limit”|Photos above 200 megapixels are refused. Downscale the photo and add it again.
“16-bit TIFF is not supported”|Export an 8-bit JPEG, PNG or TIFF first.
“The file is damaged or incomplete”|Copy or export the photo again.

Sections.Heading: Saving
Items: “Save failed: … could not be written”|The output folder is read-only, full or offline. Press **Browse** under Save to, pick a folder you can write to, and press Save selected again.
“Saved … ; … file(s) failed. Check the save log.”|Some files were written. The Log tab lists the ones that failed.
You are asked to replace files|Existing files are only replaced when you press **Replace files**. Cancel keeps them.

Sections.Heading: Engine
Items: “Engine unavailable”|Press **Retry** on the card at the bottom left. If it fails again, open Processing settings → Device details and press **Check setup**.
The engine restarted on its own|This happens after Cancel, or when a command times out, so the next operation starts clean. Results you already have are kept.
Slow or failing GPU work|Choose CPU in Processing settings, or press **Use CPU** under Device details.

Sections.Heading: Results
Items: Good mean ΔE, poor-looking photos|Check the Max ΔE and the validation line. Look for clipping, glare, mixed lighting, or a different input color space.
FFC artifacts|Check the white reference for objects or marks, and that it matches the framing. Compare with FFC off.

Title: Color spaces and ICC
Summary: Tell the app how your pixels are encoded.

Items: Your photos are not plain sRGB, or you need output in another RGB space.

Sections.Heading: Steps
Items: Open **Correction settings** (gear next to CC) and find COLOR SPACES.
Set **Input space** and **Input white** to describe the pixels you supply. Set **Target space** and **Target white** for the output.
Leave both at sRGB / D65 unless you know otherwise.

Sections.Heading: Good to know
Items: With sRGB/D65 input, embedded ICC profiles are converted to working sRGB before correction. Photos without a profile are treated as sRGB.
Other input choices use the stored pixels as they are and skip ICC conversion.
FFC, GC and WB need sRGB/D65 input. For other inputs, convert first or use CC alone. Unsupported combinations are refused, not guessed.
Previews are converted for display; exported files keep the encoding you chose. Non-sRGB exports need software that reads that encoding. EXIF rotation is applied everywhere.

Title: Python and automation
Summary: Run the same pipeline from scripts and notebooks.

Items: The engine behind the app also accepts commands without a window. The Python SDK in the python/ folder wraps it; Python is optional for the desktop app. Read api/README.md beside the application.
A minimal run: ColorCorrection(Config(save_path="results"), root=app_folder), then run(Image="chart.jpg", White_Image="Blank.JPG") and predict_images(images=["sample.jpg"]).
Use one engine per independent session and send one request at a time.
The API is a local process interface, not an internet server. The app does not open a network listener by default.

This app builds on the stepwise workflow by Wakholi and colleagues: A systematic color correction pipeline for controlled-environment imaging. The Plant Phenome Journal 9, e70067 (2026). DOI: 10.1002/ppj2.70067.

The research argues for evaluating the imaging setup together with the correction, rather than treating a regression model as a substitute for controlled capture. The app's automatic GC and NN safeguards are later developments, not a reproduction of every setting in the study.

**Original research** opens the article in your browser. **Study PDF** opens docs/research/ppj2.70067.pdf if you have placed it there. **Documentation** opens the offline docs folder, including docs/color-science-validation.md.
